units.text: In this video, you'll use three failure walkthroughs to decide where to look before retrying. Start with Lambda's asynchronous path: H T T P two oh two confirms the event entered the queue, not that the handler succeeded. A function error gets two additional attempts by default; a throttling or system error uses a different retry policy.

Follow the failure to a configured destination or dead-letter queue. Check the retained record, function logs and delivery failures; fix the underlying issue before replaying from a durable source. Replay only the affected events and make the writes idempotent so earlier successes are not duplicated.

When Lambda times out connecting to private RDS, isolate the specific network hop. Correlate the invocation with logs or a trace, then follow the path from the function's V P C networking to the database endpoint. Check the route, security rules and D N S rather than changing the timeout first.

Check the writer or reader endpoint, the engine port and the database credentials separately. A T C P timeout and a database authentication rejection point to different checks. nat or a supported V P C endpoint addresses a separate outbound path, not the private RDS login.

First separate an A P I Gateway throttle from a malformed Lambda response. For H T T P four twenty-nine, check the 429s in client or access logs where available, then examine the matching usage-plan, stage or account limits. The rest A P I metric four X X Error gives aggregate context, not an exact count of just throttles.

For a five oh two in a Lambda proxy integration, check the integration error and function logs. Compare the response with the configured format; a rest proxy response needs a valid status code and a string body. A five oh two can have other causes, so confirm the evidence before making a fix.

In this video, you'll verify where an AppSync request is allowed or denied, then decide whether to promote a canary. In the successful AppSync test, the caller may access the schema field and the resolver role may read the Dynamo D B item. Both checks must pass.

Compare the two failed tests. A caller denied at AppSync does not reach the resolver; an authorized caller can reach the resolver and still get a downstream error if the resolver role cannot access Dynamo D B. Fix the right authorization boundary instead of broadening both.

Send a small portion of requests to a candidate before exposing all users. A rest A P I stage can direct traffic to a canary deployment, while a weighted Lambda alias splits traffic between published function versions. Choose the control that matches what changed.

Compare the candidate against the baseline on server errors, P ninety five latency and business success. Use logs and alarms to validate the result. If the candidate misses the agreed thresholds, roll back traffic; promote only after the signals and the application outcome agree.

In this video, you'll optimize an entire serverless request path and use its invocation pattern to identify retry ownership. Follow the request through A P I Gateway, Lambda and Dynamo D B. Measure end-to-end cost and P ninety five latency before changing just the most visible service.

Reduce unnecessary requests or payload size at the A P I. Right-size function memory, duration and concurrency together, and match the database key and capacity to the workload. Include CloudWatch Logs retention and data transfer in the cost check. Measure after each meaningful change.

Retry ownership starts with how the function is invoked. In the synchronous A P I Gateway path, the caller sees the result and decides whether to retry. With a direct asynchronous invocation, Lambda accepts into its internal queue and manages eligible retries; configure a failure destination or dead-letter queue as appropriate.

An S Q S event source mapping polls the source queue and invokes the handler with a batch. Failed messages can return after the visibility timeout, and the queue's redrive policy governs delivery to its dead-letter queue. Use an idempotent handler regardless of who manages retry.
